cycles.title: The Watershed Kingdoms
cycles.description: The opening reach already contains working civilizations: harvest machinery, healers, councils, military depots and negotiated dragon service. Their territories grow around water and roads; these are represented societies with older histories of their own.
cycles.sequenceNote: A proposed early reach, not a primitive age or the beginning of civilization. Agricultural districts and territorial states overlap. The Eagle Queen remembers a specific century of political succession; that local transition does not date neighboring kingdoms.

eras.title: The managed watersheds
eras.description: Cisterns, mills, harvest apparatus and protective boundaries make settlement possible. Their specialists already share methods, negotiate with councils and work through material systems.
context: Agrarian work depends on built water systems and sustained specialist labor.
Solar harvesting, bounded medicine and living barriers are distinct local practices.
Councils, research and trained observers show established civic cultures.
eras.sequenceNote: These districts may coexist with the territorial states. Ninety years of barrier work, eleven flowering seasons and twenty years inside a held sunset remain different local histories.

eras.title: The roads acquire crowns
eras.description: Depots, lock tolls, passes and heat networks connect populations to rulers. Some states inherit custodial obligations; others turn service into tribute or impose military claims on living neighbors.
context: Standing armies and supply depots operate beyond a single village.
Dragon service, winter tribute and dynastic compacts distribute power across regions.
Successor crowns and reused refuges preserve traces of earlier arrangements.
eras.sequenceNote: A proposed later horizon overlaps the managed watersheds. The Eagle story specifically follows three successor crowns after a custodial queen; no other dynasty is made its descendant.

cycles.title: The Chartered Civilizations
cycles.description: Road commerce and public works sustain specialist careers: repair shops handle unlike magical devices, cities license practitioners, and schools teach disciplines that can travel beyond a ruling household. Court patronage remains powerful beside these networks.
cycles.sequenceNote: The reconstruction proposes a wider circulation of skills after the opening territorial reach. Courts, commercial roads and qualified public services overlap; rural settlements can be parts of these networks rather than an earlier developmental stage.

eras.title: The household and the workshop
eras.description: Courtly power acts through property, family expectations, printed gracework and consumer protection. Skilled workers can reproduce some practices even while rank controls whose choices count.
context: Great households and patronage govern service, property and family obligations.
Costume instructions, acoustic fittings and protective perfumery circulate through craft.
Carriages, salons and palace workshops belong to a developed courtly economy.
eras.sequenceNote: These households overlap the hired roads and licensed practice. Their separate family histories are not one dynasty or a single school of magic.

eras.title: The hired road
eras.description: A road economy supports adventurers, smiths, clerics and other traveling specialists. Inn rooms, fairs and repair benches connect settlements without making them one kingdom.
context: Coaches, caravans, inns and public hiring create a commercial travel culture.
Specialist equipment and bounded magical services support livelihoods.
Reputations and printed notices circulate farther than individual households.
eras.sequenceNote: Commercial journeys overlap courtly and professional communities rather than marking a separate universal stage. Each curse and crossing keeps its own conditions; sanctuary travel dates no other gate.

eras.title: The licensed arts
eras.description: Formal qualifications, source contracts and disciplined training turn unusual capacities into recognized work. Public works and colleges give practitioners a social place beyond heroic reputation.
context: Municipal licenses, qualifications and teaching institutions regulate practice.
Qualified surveyors travel to a mountain village; training recruits from villages, mines and noble kitchens.
Living power depends on bodily training, source conditions and exact material work.
eras.sequenceNote: Kethra’s qualification precedes her apprenticeship story directly, with an undated interval. The other stories supply a proposed city-and-periphery network of skills, not a shared college or synchronized reform.

cycles.title: The Familiar Worlds
cycles.description: One reach makes unusual capacities part of household engineering, laboratory schooling and daily commerce. Another preserves familiar phones, buses and schools while actual magic is scarce or dismissed locally. These are different public conditions within a long history, not a decline inferred from a private life.
cycles.sequenceNote: The broader public modernity before Nell and Bash’s low-magic home is an editorial reconstruction. Nell’s endpoint before later gods and the Glass Sea is established. Northbridge explicitly treats magic as old stories and effects; its placement nearby does not make the cities or years identical.

eras.title: Living magic in the household
eras.description: Ordinary electronics and domestic appliances coexist with engineered magical property and unusual biology. Families use specialist services without needing every member to share a power.
context: Phones, apartments and appliances provide the everyday material setting.
Estate repair and laboratory education accommodate living magic.
Inheritance carries objects and obligations across decades of ordinary family life.
eras.sequenceNote: Proposed before the locally quieter horizon. The pendant’s thirty-one years in storage belong to one family; the laboratory pupil’s lack of magic is not evidence of a world losing it.

eras.title: An engineered education
eras.description: Cinder Annex combines projection engines, dispatch slates and assessed construction with collaborators whose bodies are alive. Its infernal setting supplies a parallel technical culture rather than a terrestrial location.
context: Formal schooling teaches engineered magical craft and real-time dispatch.
Living moss collaborators require food, space and choices beyond their maker’s plans.
eras.sequenceNote: Attached to this reach for its advanced applied schooling. The Annex’s material-world coordinate and its side of extinction remain unresolved; its machinery supplies no route to a named terrestrial school.

eras.title: The locally hidden extraordinary
eras.description: Familiar streets continue where living magic has little place in public explanations. A private route, a dream contact and a school’s concealed defenders operate inside ordinary social infrastructure.
context: Nell and Bash return to an established old low-magic material world.
Northbridge’s city explicitly treats magic as old stories and cheap effects.
Phones, radios, family travel and translation let hidden practitioners exchange help across regions.
eras.sequenceNote: These are compatible local conditions, not proof of one synchronized civilization. Nell and Bash keep their unequal clocks; Garnet’s sixty years stay local. Attendance precedes Help by three afternoons, and their supplied sequence remains before the Bay.

cycles.title: The Inherited Kingdoms
cycles.description: Later societies inhabit accumulated histories: dragon rulers redesign governments to outlast them, harbor rites assign bounded duties, and trade adapts to unusual ecologies. Beside these institutions, forests reclaim masonry and ancient refuges preserve practices whose surrounding kingdoms have disappeared.
cycles.sequenceNote: This proposed reach follows the old low-magic period into later visible powers. Its regions have different clocks and inheritances. A recovered woodland, a mortuary temple and two dragon governments can share a broad horizon without sharing a collapse, species lineage or source of power.

eras.title: Government beyond its dragons
eras.description: Two distinct collectives of twelve dragons have spent about two centuries managing human polities. Both seek durable institutions that permit sleep, but their disguises, worship and departures differ.
context: Kharost rotates forty-seven fabricated royal masks over 218 years and retires that state worship.
Varkesh’s worshipped living guise is a collective god; abdication ends its sovereign divinity.
Grain, water, archives and succession procedures must function without a ruler always awake.
eras.sequenceNote: Independent government experiments placed in an overlapping horizon. Borrowed constitutional ideas are a historical possibility, not an identified exchange. Neither the dragons nor their godhood are interchangeable.

eras.title: The harbor and its gods
eras.description: Coastal communities make divine jurisdiction specific to harbor work, release, protection and ritual responsibility. Old records can preserve duties while losing the instructions that make them safe.
context: Boat work, grain traffic and shared water infrastructure sustain mature coastal societies.
Worship and jurisdiction give living powers bounded public duties.
Repeated rites and damaged instructions carry obligations across generations.
eras.sequenceNote: These ports share a proposed maritime culture, not named gods or one harbor. Orselle’s eighty-six years of agelessness precede fifty-seven minutes in office; Brackwater’s prior circuits follow their own calendar.

eras.title: The Salt Crucible
eras.description: An established religious order faces the bodily and social costs of opposed callings.
context: Religious vows and publicly recognized supernatural roles structure the conflict.
The crisis acts through living people and a local source of power.
eras.sequenceNote: Placed alongside public religious institutions, not after a particular divine government. This local crisis is not the universal extinction.

eras.title: The long afterlives
eras.description: Current lives occupy places left behind by earlier states. Forest grows through reused foundations; a wizard remembers imperial trade; a dragon mortuary becomes shelter for the living.
context: Roads, farm walls, orchards and ruins become new ecological ground over many generations.
A two-thousand-year-old tower preserves memories of empires a passing craft worker cannot identify.
An ancient mortuary apparatus is adapted to protect young refugees.
eras.sequenceNote: The deep roots precede each story’s present, often by thousands of local years. Their later placement is a proposal about accumulated inheritance; no common empire, evacuation or collapse joins the three places.

eras.title: Trade at the changing edges
eras.description: A paid ice dragon joins desert water work, a new monster industry imports expertise, and an armed survey threatens a hidden seed community. Trade and extraction bring unlike knowledge into contact.
context: Copper condensers, established roads and paid specialist work serve a desert settlement.
Monster materials rapidly enter roofs, ropes, clinics and lamps; foreign experts know dangers locals have only begun to observe.
Maps and survey expeditions can expose communities that have reasons to stay outside trade routes.
eras.sequenceNote: These regional frontiers overlap older governments and refuges. The monster industry is only three months old inside a much older trade culture. Neither its newness nor an undocumented water effect establishes a universal stage.

cycles.title: The Public Sky and the Bay
cycles.description: Another familiar urban reach accommodates visible powers in transport, weather work and civic defense. The Bay story looks back on a monarchy formed centuries earlier and circles that have since faded; its aftermath passes through damaged recovery records into later museum memory.
cycles.sequenceNote: The public-sky horizon is proposed before the battle’s last-survivor society. Not About That’s reading position before the Bay is supplied; Brackenport’s relative date is editorial. The Bay arc preserves its direct sequence and centuries without treating them as whole Galactic Cycles.

eras.title: The inhabited public sky
eras.description: Public powers share modern roads, shipping, schools and communication systems. One city negotiates extraordinary force at its harbor; another community treats magical flight as everyday work.
context: Phones, trams, buses and modern shipping form ordinary civic infrastructure.
Magical flight serves deliveries and agriculture as well as defense.
Publicly visible powers meet local governance without establishing a common hero registry.
eras.sequenceNote: An earlier horizon than the Bay’s sole surviving monarch in this reconstruction. Brackenport’s nine years and the crowded-sky afternoon are not dated against one another. No named school, city or power lineage links them.

eras.title: A crown spent, a record inherited
eras.description: Centuries of monarchy end with a crown spent in battle. Modern recovery systems then misidentify an ordinary prisoner; much later a museum must distinguish a surviving witness from the civic legend.
context: Independent circles negotiated Solstice’s coronation centuries before the battle; no living subjects remain at the Bay.
Damaged archives and a booking scan produce the aftermath’s false identification.
Generations of commemorative tradition intervene before Solstice visits the museum.
eras.sequenceNote: Solstice → Dress → Count follows the supplied reading sequence; Count explicitly follows the Bay by centuries. The prisoner is a different woman. The museum’s side of extinction stays open despite this proposed pre-extinction location.

cycles.title: The Layered Worlds
cycles.description: Whole societies depend on systems built by earlier lives: predictive flood guarantees, municipal wards, a centralized solar network, buried routes and a body mistaken for permanent ground. This late reach contains active invention as well as inherited danger. The final Ascendancy still connects vigorous magical civilizations when the Array ends all old power.
cycles.sequenceNote: The Glass Sea follows the earlier modernities and Bay. Other system-dependent and archaeological societies overlap here by proposal, not a shared disaster. Their different origins remain open; All Accounts Due alone establishes the universal terminal boundary.

eras.title: The governed landscape
eras.description: Cities and regional states distribute survival through living magical infrastructure. Public authorities decide who benefits from prediction, protection and stored responsibility.
context: Large populations depend on civic networks maintained through active living powers.
Government, records and technical specialists organize the distribution of risk.
Flood management, district protection and solar infrastructure operate at a landscape scale.
eras.sequenceNote: A proposed later reach of system-dependent civilizations, with no mutual order among the three polities. Sablewake’s local centuries and the Glass Sea’s four hundred years remain distinct; no shared energy system is inferred.

eras.title: The structures become the ground
eras.description: Mine workings encounter an older maintained fire bridge; explorers enter an immense route lattice; towns occupy a colossus recorded as dead. Earlier works have become the physical conditions of later lives.
context: Present mines, expeditions and settlements meet material structures older than their own knowledge.
Some old infrastructure remains actively maintained; other origins are lost even after a thousand years of local records.
Survey, skilled observation and repair work matter more than a reliable founding account.
eras.sequenceNote: Three different forms of inheritance share a proposed horizon. The fire bridge is not the labyrinth or the colossus, and the latter’s recorded death is no verified explanation. Their older layers remain unplotted.

eras.title: The final accounting
eras.description: A world of walking cities, route dragons, graft medicine, gravity craft and inner fire still works. Three centuries of Array construction and decades of stolen conditions converge on the act that ends every old material magic.
context: The Ascendancy’s armistice joins vigorous route, furnace and civic systems before extinction.
The Array develops for 302 years; Faris accumulates bounded living conditions over thirty-one years.
The six then-active roots end here; they are not assigned as the origin of every earlier magical practice.
eras.sequenceNote: Fixed extinction anchor: old material magic ends here, followed by perfect zero.

cycles.title: The Weight of Human Hands
cycles.description: The world continues through perfect material zero. A reactor city remembers magic as long dead; guilds, workshops and traveling communities build lives from machinery, ordinary organisms and bodily capacities. Industrial and road-bound regions keep different fortunes within the same broad reach.
cycles.sequenceNote: The first represented Long Dark reach is not its first generation. Civic engineering and dispersed territorial power overlap as regional fortunes vary; the layout does not make every road polity a successor to Orison.

eras.title: The reactor city
eras.description: Four million people depend on Orison’s ancient fission reactors and powered magnetic rings. Hospitals, trains and district evacuation make maintenance a matter of citywide survival.
context: A metropolitan population depends on inherited nuclear and electromagnetic infrastructure.
Operators maintain complex physical systems in a culture that remembers magic as long dead.
Public services and emergency movement depend on the same vulnerable city machinery.
eras.sequenceNote: Advanced engineering already exists in this early represented Long Dark reach. Orison’s date relative to the workshops and road societies is unestablished; neither a shared collapse nor a shared origin is implied.

eras.title: The workshop networks
eras.description: Repair benches, guild works and practical assays sustain skilled livelihoods. Expertise travels through services and trades, with physical devices and ordinary organisms doing the work.
context: Maintained mechanisms and measured physical behavior support ordinary work.
Guilds, workshops and service trades distribute technical expertise.
Practical knowledge answers a customer’s problem or a local material need.
eras.sequenceNote: These workshop and guild societies overlap the proposed reactor-city and road horizons. Their smaller working scale does not make them ancestors or descendants of Orison; no common engineering tradition is established.

eras.title: Roads between unlike peoples
eras.description: A caravan crosses out of a village whose ordinary strength means something different elsewhere. Serpentfolk caves and inhabited underground passages lie beyond the assumptions carried by travelers.
context: Caravans, roads and rescue routes connect populations with different bodily capacities.
Physical labor and local knowledge matter more than a traveler's inherited labels.
A neighboring community can be misread without belonging to an earlier age.
eras.sequenceNote: These dispersed societies can coexist with the engineering centers. Their biology and travel economies support a shared regional horizon; no common species, kingdom or caravan route is established.

cycles.title: Crowns Along the Signal Roads
cycles.description: Royal power reaches through roads, lamps, mirrors and local expertise. Some courts try to enclose lives within palace authority; smaller polities and civic institutions preserve other sources of power. These societies make an inhabited political landscape, with cities and countryside keeping different fortunes.
cycles.sequenceNote: This is a proposed later reach of territorial states and distributed civic infrastructure. Optical relays distinguish its closest cluster from the bodily travel stories in the preceding reach. Regional courts can rise or fall independently; no one empire or common network is implied.

eras.title: The imperial household
eras.description: Palace decisions extend into armies, capitals and family life. Succession, household obligations and limits on a ruler’s authority shape public power, while practical rescue still comes down to tools and labor.
context: Rulers, capitals and standing military forces give households public reach.
Marriage, inheritance, witnessed succession and returning relatives affect territorial authority.
Physical travel, weapons and manual work dominate the represented action.
eras.sequenceNote: Palace and town histories overlap without one imperial succession. The capital’s seventeen-year absence and the vacant throne’s fifteen years remain local. The Vacant Throne’s side of extinction is unresolved; Save That Dragon is also tentative because its dragon’s fire is unclassified.

eras.title: The signal kingdoms and civic towns
eras.description: Courts depend on relays, local keepers and negotiated public works. Towns also organize membership, skilled instruction and household care through durable civic institutions.
context: Duskglass mirrors and hushglass relays carry political information through maintained physical networks.
Small kingdoms control indispensable local knowledge and negotiate with royal centers.
Houses, civic yards and hired care give settled towns institutions beyond the palace.
eras.sequenceNote: The two relay-state stories form this horizon's closest material comparison: both make crowns depend on distributed civic work. Their optical systems and kingdoms are distinct. The other towns may coexist around such states; the elf caretaker's two-century career remains her own local past.

cycles.title: A Familiar Meridian
cycles.description: Another long reach contains recognizably modern streets: festivals, cafés, phones and ordinary private lives. Closed borders can conceal a neighboring city’s electric transport; elsewhere, private engineering reaches from a household workshop into orbit.
cycles.sequenceNote: The familiar present is one region of an immense material history. Unequal neighboring societies can coexist, and advanced engineering need not follow ordinary modern life. The proposed horizon joins material and institutional contexts without dating these communities to one present.

eras.title: The familiar street
eras.description: Modern services and institutions support domestic lives and encounters across closed borders. Electric streets, familiar transport and commercial travel can coexist with a neighbor’s very different expectations.
context: Familiar modern technology and everyday urban or domestic institutions frame the living scenes.
Relationships, employment and bodily life require no operative material magic.
Five centuries of closed borders conceal a neighboring modern society in one story; the difference is geographic within its present.
eras.sequenceNote: These familiar societies have no established mutual order. The scouts’ local five-century interval does not establish a lost technological age. Ruth’s material life alone is placed here, while her station retains an unresolved afterlife coordinate.

eras.title: Engineering within familiar lives
eras.description: A private engineer holds orbital leverage, while an inventive household rebuilds the machine from its first date. Technical reach can become politically significant without making daily rooms, meals and relationships unfamiliar.
context: Advanced material engineering coexists with ordinary domestic life.
Private technical work ranges from a household machine to control of satellites.
Personal relationships shape the use of expertise without establishing a common industry or state.
eras.sequenceNote: These proposed technical societies overlap the familiar streets. The anniversary household and satellite dispute have no established mutual order or shared program; orbital capability is already present within this reach.

cycles.title: The Manufactured Citizen
cycles.description: Technical civilizations make bodies, identity and perception into services—and assets institutions can own or command. Domestic manufacture, reconstructed rulers, controlled cities and military systems draw the boundary of personhood differently.
cycles.sequenceNote: This reach is proposed around institutions that manufacture or administer identity. Domestic, commercial, civic and military arrangements overlap. Its later position does not establish a technological advance over every earlier society or descent from the familiar meridian.

eras.title: Modified neighbourhoods
eras.description: Bionics and cognitive engineering enter ordinary neighborhoods. A repair kiosk and a neighbor's filtered cognition show the services and restrictions that accompany manufactured capabilities.
context: Bionic or synthetic bodies are present in domestic and neighborhood settings.
Repair work, private services and ordinary urban institutions support daily life.
Personhood is negotiated through familiar social encounters as well as technical care.
eras.sequenceNote: Domestic manufacture can coexist with consumer reconstruction, controlled cities and military systems. These households have no established mutual order or common service provider.

eras.title: Reconstructed lives
eras.description: Commercial, medical and political systems can revise appearance, rebuild combatants or grow rulers from ancient genetic sources. A manufactured body does not settle who owns its future.
context: Genetic modification and bodily reconstruction are technically developed.
Medical, commercial and political institutions mediate access to altered bodies and identities.
Physical reconstruction can reproduce traits without recovering a vanished person’s memories.
eras.sequenceNote: These distinct reconstruction societies overlap other technical regions without an established mutual order. The queen’s roughly ten-thousand-year historical gap, nineteen years of development and sixty-year imperial career are local intervals, not Galactic Cycles.

eras.title: The city that accounts for you
eras.description: Data systems decide who can move, remain housed, be recognized or possess a history. Registration can control access even when the city’s buildings are engineered living tissue.
context: Networks and automated urban services govern movement, housing or public knowledge.
Institutions claim authority through registration, visibility or control of records.
Excluded residents and censored histories expose the limits of apparently complete civic knowledge.
eras.sequenceNote: Pervasive control is a regional political arrangement within the technical horizon, not a necessary later stage. Each city has its own present and concealed past; no common administration is established.

eras.title: Commanded lives
eras.description: Military and civic systems treat bodies and experience as deployable assets. Operators confront the difference between executing a command and retaining a life.
context: Engineered command systems control combat, defense or deployable bodies.
Institutional programming can outlast peace, service or the wishes of the person inside it.
Human decisions and bodily limits remain consequential within advanced machinery.
eras.sequenceNote: Control systems coexist with civilian embodiment and unequal cities. A retired dispatcher, a war android and a displaced pilot have separate institutional histories. None shares a military program or enemy; the Jovian watch belongs with the maintained orbital habitats.

cycles.title: The Inhabited Ruins
cycles.description: Technical histories survive unevenly through inhabited remains, salvage and working cities. Some communities recover forgotten works; others sustain environmental infrastructure and migrating traditions in an active present.
cycles.sequenceNote: This proposed reach places incomplete historical knowledge beside functioning civic systems. Loss and continuity vary by region; its cities are not all rebuildings after one collapse, and their capabilities do not set a universal technological level.

eras.title: The buried territories
eras.description: Descendants and salvagers read material remains with incomplete inherited knowledge. Their discoveries reveal how unevenly a civilization’s past can survive.
context: Lost technical histories persist through sealed works, ruins and salvage.
Present communities recover or interpret remnants through practical exploration.
A recovered structure does not identify the origin or fate of every surrounding society.
eras.sequenceNote: Lost knowledge can coexist with functioning technical cities elsewhere. The room’s two local stages stay together; its descendants and the salvage expedition have no established mutual order or common catastrophe.

eras.title: The living city
eras.description: Ecology, climate and collective resources become working infrastructure. Mature technical systems coexist with varied building traditions and inherited routes.
context: Material engineering supports buildings, water and environmental management.
Cities and communities negotiate common resources through everyday institutions.
Different local forms and advanced technology can share a present.
eras.sequenceNote: These civic systems overlap the proposed ruined territories. Their order is unknown; condensation, seasonal routes and materially varied foundations do not establish descent from a common lost city or require surviving old magic.

cycles.title: The World Beneath Its Sky
cycles.description: Communities inhabit the world’s orbital and stellar surroundings as well as its ground. Working cargo routes, inherited mechanisms and ancient human roads preserve different histories; surface and space societies need not rise or fall together.
cycles.sequenceNote: A late represented reach of working and inherited orbital infrastructure, with overlapping horizons. This is not the first space age: earlier reaches already contain satellites and orbital shields. Builders and departures stay undated, with no common exodus; reawakening lies beyond this material reach.

eras.title: Divided sky and ground
eras.description: Orbit and ground preserve incompatible accounts of a shared inhabited world. A supposedly dead surface sends its own words; a dinosaur council answers hazardous human descents with measured signals.
context: Human orbital populations and surface communities occupy the same physical environment.
Inherited maps, scripts and official accounts fail to keep pace with living populations.
Practical signaling can establish contact before either side shares a history or language.
eras.sequenceNote: The two encounters share a proposed horizon of divided orbital and ground knowledge. The claimed 812-year surface abandonment belongs only to the reed-and-radiator exchange. It does not date the dinosaurs, identify either station population or establish a common exodus.

eras.title: The maintained sky
eras.description: Crews sustain occupied space through cargo work, repairs, thermal margins and physical ecological management. Inherited mechanisms and present-day flight equipment both impose practical limits.
context: Occupied stations, cargo routes and surface grids require continuous technical work.
Docking, crew rescue and thermal or ecological hazards shape daily decisions.
Crews use distinct safety systems and inherited structures without establishing one builder or space program.
eras.sequenceNote: This orbital-work horizon overlaps divided ground societies. Jupiter’s thirty-year watch, the terrestrial sunshade and the cargo tug have no established mutual order. The tug’s one-charge neural restoration leaves outside momentum and consequences unchanged.

eras.title: The old stellar roads
eras.description: Old spacefaring infrastructure meets grounded life, and people encounter humanity as something already carried through a very long history.
context: Ancient spacefaring works or routes remain materially consequential.
Present travelers and grounded communities interpret inherited human traces.
Technical observation connects local lives to histories beyond the surface.
eras.sequenceNote: The root burn is followed here by a proposed age of fragmented stellar travel, represented by the ship over Ruskala. Their common network is unestablished and the ship's memory damage has no known cause. The connection is a historical hypothesis, while each story's internal sequence is explicit.

cycles.title: The Returning World
cycles.description: The first reciprocal working ends perfect zero. After an unmeasured interval, rural livelihoods, hereditary states and technical towns have learned distinct ways to live with active powers. Their institutions meet different local needs, from a sheepfold to a city’s spellwrights.
cycles.sequenceNote: The return is the fixed boundary; the later overlapping societies are proposed contexts, not the next generation or descendants of one another. New workings do not restore the six old roots. No universal ascent from village to court to workshop is implied.

eras.title: The first link
eras.description: Ordinary light reaches a living encounter and the first reciprocal working begins.
context: The established chronology ends perfect zero at this encounter.
The new working depends on a living reciprocal relation and does not restore an old system.
eras.sequenceNote: Fixed reawakening anchor. The earlier fall belongs to the extinction endpoint; its carried light crosses the Long Dark.

eras.title: The common workings
eras.description: Local craft and rural life have learned to deal with active living power. Names, timber and everyday livelihoods carry obligations that must be worked out in person.
context: Small communities and local trades organize daily life.
Living magical effects act through practical relationships rather than mass technical systems.
Craft work and reciprocity determine what a person can safely ask of a working.
eras.sequenceNote: A mature local horizon after the first link, with time for inherited buildings and established practice. Its rural regions can coexist with courts and technical craft; the Hollow Cask’s twelve-week plan stays local.

eras.title: The ritual kingdoms
eras.description: Hereditary states recognize living rites, magical professions and unusual creatures as political facts. Regional communities must negotiate those powers in succession, public service and war.
context: Hereditary governments and settled regional communities structure public authority.
Active living rites, creature capacities and magical professionals affect civic decisions.
Long local records and practical travel or siege work coexist with supernatural power.
eras.sequenceNote: Ritual states overlap common workings and specialist craft, rather than following every village. Forecasting’s three centuries, suspended injury and Shalegate’s three-night siege remain separate local spans.

eras.title: Craft before divine claims
eras.description: Skilled workers bring practical knowledge to encounters with apparent or actual divinity. Bodies, tools and civic damage put limits on what higher status can accomplish.
context: Experienced manual specialists use bodily knowledge and practical tools.
Inhabited settlements and built works bear the consequences of unusual powers.
The action depends on bounded material or living conditions, even when a participant claims divine authority.
eras.sequenceNote: A technical civic horizon alongside ritual states and rural life. The regenerating claimant and the god of death have no established mutual order, common species, theology or mechanism.

eras.title: The mill room
eras.description: A working mill town encounters a growing machine whose apparent observers claim a higher perspective.
context: Mill repair, couriers, ledgers and physical routes organize the settlement.
Residents use experiments and practical engineering to investigate an intrusive mechanism.
eras.sequenceNote: The mill town overlaps the represented craft societies without an established sequence. Its active-era attachment remains tentative; the machine’s ontology and the apparent players’ external coordinate are unresolved.

cycles.title: The Inherited Streets
cycles.description: New workings have become embedded in electrified streets, old thresholds, family objects and household customs. Particular keepers preserve practical knowledge across generations, while modern services and ordinary neighbors live around obligations whose histories they only partly know.
cycles.sequenceNote: Local custodianship is this reach's historical context; personal privacy cannot date a civilization. Its overlapping modern societies may also have public powers elsewhere. The broad placement is editorial, while family intervals, remembered debts and the unresolved coordinates of external realms remain intact.

eras.title: Old workings under ordinary streets
eras.description: Existing buildings, local promises and unofficial routes keep operating inside modern towns. Public redevelopment and everyday travel meet knowledge held in particular places rather than a common account of the supernatural.
context: Vehicles, electric services and redevelopment belong to the ordinary civic fabric.
Local obligations, thresholds and route conditions survive through families or custodians.
Different workings retain their own access rules and histories.
eras.sequenceNote: These towns share a broad proposed horizon with household and concealed capacities. Their mutual order is open; the promise, threshold and bus route are not one mechanism or transport network.

eras.title: Household keepers
eras.description: Families inherit companions, instruments and relations with durable powers. Their knowledge lives in particular domestic arrangements, beside schools and services that continue their ordinary routines.
context: Inherited objects or relationships carry locally specific powers.
Authority and practical knowledge remain with households and particular agents.
Modern domestic life continues around those arrangements.
eras.sequenceNote: These households overlap the local street workings; they are not their later stage. The Fenwick activations, audit Tuesdays and later overwrite retain one family sequence, without dating the cat or the grandmother.

eras.title: Encounters without a public account
eras.description: A familiar school, home, road or apartment frames an extraordinary encounter for which the people involved have no adequate shared explanation. The evidence describes their local situation, without proving that every surrounding institution is ignorant.
context: Ordinary contemporary homes, schools and roads provide the material frame.
Effects are encountered or interpreted privately rather than through an identified public profession.
The origin, larger distribution or external coordinates of the working remain unsettled.
eras.sequenceNote: The living frames overlap other modern contexts and have no established mutual order. Four dawns and the road trip’s altered clocks stay local; Ryo’s home frame alone is placed, with every assignment destination undated.

eras.title: Behind the familiar face
eras.description: Nonhuman capacities sit beside ordinary school, work and family life. Several inhabitants deliberately pass as ordinary people; rescue or friendship can bring a previously hidden identity into one person’s knowledge.
context: Modern school, work, transport and household routines continue around unusual bodies.
Shapeshifting and divine identity are explicitly concealed in some of these communities.
A private disclosure does not establish either universal secrecy or a shared species.
eras.sequenceNote: These households occupy an overlapping proposed modern horizon. A few explicitly hide their nature; others negotiate an unfamiliar encounter. Such private boundaries do not date the wider society's recognition of powers, and the comparison with publicly ordinary wings remains an echo.

eras.title: Private continuities
eras.description: Living hosts and family practices maintain particular relationships across changes of body or death. Access is negotiated person by person, with consequences that ordinary family obligations cannot settle for them.
context: Living people maintain access through a host relay or a household practice.
Consent, custody and the continuity of a person are practical local questions.
Neither practice identifies a universal afterlife administration or common mechanism.
eras.sequenceNote: Placed alongside other modern household arrangements without an established mutual order. Thirteen years of searching and decades-dead relatives are local histories; no earlier body, death or external endpoint gains a cycle coordinate.

eras.title: College across the gate
eras.description: A private infernal passage reaches a human engineering college. Family authority meets admissions, accommodation and emergency-contact requirements at one material endpoint.
context: Communications and a human engineering college establish a contemporary material endpoint.
A particular gate gives one family access across realms.
Ordinary paperwork and clinical limits shape the student’s practical independence.
eras.sequenceNote: Only the human college frame is placed among these modern societies. The infernal realm retains an unresolved coordinate; a private gate and an unprepared ordinary clinic do not prove this society precedes specialist crossing services elsewhere.

cycles.title: The Civic Powers
cycles.description: Colleges, patrols, clinics, museums and expedition crews organize around extraordinary abilities and inherited workings. Households still improvise their own accommodations; public infrastructure can also carry coercive power, and professional accounts of the past can fail when confronted by living people.
cycles.sequenceNote: This proposed later reach concentrates institutional capacity around powers, alongside continuing household traditions and covert lives. Its regions share neither one government nor one revelation. The excavation's advanced arrival frame sits farther within this reach; the vanished village's departure remains unplaced.

eras.title: Bodies in everyday life
eras.description: Bodily capacities and unpredictable workings fit into recognizable streets and household routines. Locally ordinary wings, adapted equipment and care during illness involve different practical accommodations.
context: Grown, inherited and built wings are recognized everyday possibilities in one community.
Radios, tools and domestic arrangements accommodate particular capacities or uncontrolled workings.
Household adaptations and ordinary nursing advice do not establish one specialist institution or shared public status.
eras.sequenceNote: These households overlap organized extraordinary work and practices of care. Their mutual order is unresolved; wings, shrinking and illness-triggered workings retain different mechanisms and limits.

eras.title: Organized extraordinary work
eras.description: Colleges, patrols and established hero or villain identities make power a recognizable occupation. The people inside those institutions still have ordinary friendships, injuries, marriages and family disputes.
context: Formal training and established hero or villain roles organize public expectations.
Equipment, response habits and professional identities continue into domestic life.
The institutions have local histories rather than one shared founding.
eras.sequenceNote: This professional horizon overlaps ordinary accommodations and specialized care. No internal order is established among these stories, and none is asserted to continue Northbridge or the Bay across extinction.

eras.title: Care at the limits of ordinary life
eras.description: Clinical work, specialist equipment and negotiated support address extraordinary experiences without complete explanations. Practitioners and families respond to displacement, altered aging, dangerous crossings and memories whose origins remain uncertain.
context: An onset and location tag helps staff respond to involuntary travel.
A recurring memory-therapy practice separates ordinary recording from a practitioner’s faculty.
Licensed crossing staff and a clinic beside one return tunnel support monitored treatment.
Clinical aging estimates and family accommodations address one traveler’s lasting injuries without explaining all of his experienced time.
eras.sequenceNote: These practices overlap household accommodation and organized power; their order is unknown. Specialist services need not postdate an unprepared clinic elsewhere. Only the human care frames are placed: Deepmarket, the patient’s earlier memories and the lightning journey’s internal duration remain unresolved.

eras.title: Managing hazardous inheritances
eras.description: Museum agents and coastal specialists bring records, instruments and limited procedures to old objects and environments that still act on the present. Their institutions can investigate without possessing a complete account of the past.
context: Records and specialist teams organize access to inherited hazards.
Survey instruments, containment equipment and ordinary material limits guide field work.
Old structures and objects remain active without an established common origin.
eras.sequenceNote: Placed within the public-service horizon alongside domestic and professional lives. The house inspection and coastal expedition have no established mutual order; the makers, sinking and anomaly remain undated.

eras.title: The excavation beyond the village
eras.description: A mechanized excavation encounters a living village that its civilization had known through stratigraphy and myth. Emergency accommodation exposes the gap between possessing a deep record and understanding the people it describes.
context: Jointed excavation machines, stepped galleries and organized freight and care facilities support the later society.
Deep stratigraphic knowledge places the village millions of years after its departure.
A living arrival disrupts a historical identification rather than confirming it.
eras.sequenceNote: The arrival occupies a proposed farther technical reach that can overlap other public institutions. Only this endpoint is placed; the village’s departure, transport mechanism and absolute interval endpoints remain unresolved.

eras.title: The coerced broadcast city
eras.description: A modern industrial city is forced to receive predictive broadcasts. Ordinary recovery crews and urban services continue under a local power that turns private suffering into public leverage.
context: Radios, freight work, garages and recovery crews provide a modern industrial setting.
A city-wide broadcast compels public attention to a locally specific power.
The working’s coercive use differs from the institutions accommodating bodies and care.
eras.sequenceNote: A regional regime overlapping this public-power reach, not the inevitable next stage of its professions. Its predictions and blood-linked practice are local, with no shared mechanism or established order relative to the other cities.

cycles.title: The Inherited Body
cycles.description: Two further societies organize everyday expectations around population-wide bodily conventions. One makes birth channels central to craft and clinical work; another expects a true-form change at eighteen. These are distinct conditions of life, separated here across a long proposed reach.
cycles.sequenceNote: One Galactic Cycle can contain many societies and changes. Disjoint horizons keep the birthmark and eighteenth-year conventions separate; their order and unmeasured interval are proposed. Population-wide bodily expectations are their social context, not proof of a later evolutionary stage or descent from the Civic Powers.

eras.title: The birth-marked society
eras.description: An industrial society organizes craft, family expectations and clinical intervention around the marks every child is born carrying.
context: Universal ink-like birth patterns shape faculties in this society.
Dye workshops, inspection lamps and graft clinics make those faculties part of ordinary work.
A suspected absence of a mark has social and medical consequences.
eras.sequenceNote: A distinct proposed bodily horizon. Its birth-channel convention is not assigned to earlier modern societies or merged with the later eighteenth-year convention; the graft consultation remains one pre-dawn local event.

eras.title: The eighteenth-year society
eras.description: A later society has built family preparation, school records and ordinary expectations around a universal change at eighteen. The form remains personal even where the timing is shared.
context: Everyone expects a true-form change at eighteen, including changes of body size, shape or sex.
Families prepare adaptable clothing and rooms, while institutions amend personal records.
Unusual outcomes still exceed the accommodations already available.
eras.sequenceNote: Kept in a separate, later proposed horizon because its population-wide convention differs from birth channels. No common mechanism or transition event is established; one birthday and its immediate aftermath stay local.

where-the-white-elk-went.note: The story present follows hall dismantling, farm walls, orchard growth, oaks, a later road and beech. A storm finally opens an old foundation to living roots. This is a proposed post-civilizational woodland, not an earliest untouched forest.

the-last-flames.note: Stillfire’s mortuary apparatus predates remembered kingdoms; Alexstrasza adapts stored final sensations and old flues to shelter sixty-one young dragons. Its long technical inheritance belongs beside later refuges, with no identified cause shared by other regions.

the-villages-only-mage.note: Lanternscrape’s mill, cistern and road depend on a local mage, but three qualified outside surveyors bring distinct instruments and methods. The village fits a professional network’s rural reach; their synchronized tests expose a coordination problem.

the-ninety-year-barrier.note: Ninety years of the witch’s work precede the child’s breach. A small community depends on sustained personal protection across that whole local interval.

every-flower-she-knew.note: Eleven flowering seasons precede one storm-bound harvest. Local plant knowledge and bounded medicine support this agrarian placement; the effect’s underlying category remains unsettled.

blood-types-of-immortality.note: Nine years of blood research proceed through weather instruments, living samples and negotiated access. The work is a local practitioner’s history, not the origin of later healing institutions.

tea-for-the-first-guest.note: A tower roughly 2,012 years old preserves memories of imperial leaf duties, relay horses and grain fleets. The visiting bookmender cannot identify those empires. Its present belongs among surviving places whose older political worlds are uncertain.

the-unfinished-sunset.note: Mineral panes and copper rails supported collective solar harvesting before a lord’s seizure trapped the village in forty-three minutes of sunset. Twenty outside years pass while its inhabitants remember the repetition.

the-lions-last-constellation.note: Nemea’s orchard, spring, council and witnessed actions place her champion’s work in a local civic landscape. Her bronze sash and bounded task do not require the later phone-and-school magical-girl institutions.

never-a-mascot.note: Seven years of war precede a field action involving fuse carts, ordinary medicine and an independently acting rooster. Its dawn enlargement does not make it a royal mascot; both armies and civilians share one road.

when-the-eagle-bowed.note: A hundred years after the custodial Eagle Queen’s execution, three successor crowns issue incompatible warrants. Her return encounters changed watercourses and living towns; the story supplies a concrete local succession rather than generic dynastic memory.

the-gentlest-terror.note: Noble-dragon alliances provide watch, rescue, nest care and cistern maintenance. A new queen restores the right to refuse service against an inherited practice of intimidation; the region already has mature reciprocal infrastructure.

strength-of-ten.note: Ninepin is explicitly pre-extinction. The five-day deployment and return before day twenty remain one campaign within a territorial state dependent on an individual’s bounded bodily power.

the-bride-who-came-back.note: A century of annual bridal tribute supports a kingdom-wide Crown Hearth heat network. The latest bride breaks the winter-glass cycle and returns across the ice; the resulting city damage remains a consequence, not a clean liberation of every dependent household.

the-vacant-throne.note: Fifteen years of vacancy end through witnessed succession, bounded regency and the surrender of emergency military authority. Placed provisionally with these legal and military court societies; the story’s side of the extinction remains unestablished. The absence of an enacted working does not prove a magicless age.

mother-of-monsters.note: The sanctuary has accumulated refugees before an army arrives with sappers, charges and siege work. Protection becomes territorial politics through the practical problem of moving and sheltering people.

the-kingdom-of-later.note: Courtly rank and the kingdom’s settled habits reach into household time and everyday obligations. Its society fits the patronage reaches of the chartered civilizations.

the-shape-of-mercy.note: A mage lineage has mature expectations about its children’s powers. Household status and inherited access give the change its public consequences.

the-sister-behind-her-smile.note: Palace copper acoustic fittings and printed gracework instructions make this coercive costume part of a reproducible craft culture. The wearer escapes a six-day constraint before its seventh-dawn binding; servants then press practical changes.

a-note-of-spite.note: Carriages, candlelit salons and protective perfumery place the birthday dispute in a commercial court culture. The voice hex works through living warmth and has specific consumer defenses.

the-second-wearing.note: An apartment, treatment calls and a vibrating timer establish the modern household present. The pendant was boxed for thirty-one years according to its label and the niece’s family history; its inability to measure that interval does not erase the evidence.

the-last-thing-i-could-fix.note: The smith’s reputation depends on developed magical craft, traveling clients and heroic equipment. A commercial repair culture places the bench within the hired road economy.

where-it-hurts.note: The emotional-wounding sword already has a reputation among adventurers. Its bounded operation belongs to a specialist travel culture, with no established relation to other military workings.

the-seventh-night.note: The recurring curse follows a working adventurer through local journeys and lodging. Its seven-night cycle stays within the commercial travel era.

clerics-infernal-ex.note: Sanctuary service, travel and a kiln court meet through bearer-powered crossings. Only the living story frame is placed among road professions; the route retains its own conditions.

fourth-house.note: A licensed practitioner works through source contracts and clay-pipe infrastructure. The challenged three-house classification is a professional and civic system, not an ordinary school-house assignment.

voice-of-silence.note: Kethra’s examination establishes her archmage qualification within a formal institution. The direct continuation places her teaching story afterward in the same career, without a measured interval.

a-lock-on-the-inside.note: The same qualified archmage takes a mistreated apprentice and uses her call-link practice. This follows Voice of Silence within Kethra’s local professional life.

the-weight-of-falling-up-rune-shoes.note: A collegiate assessment combines roof-level flying, brooms and worked leather shoes. Rune craft and formal qualification fit the period’s licensed institutions.

the-healers-measure.note: A nominal twenty-four-month curriculum, extended to twenty-seven in this case, draws recruits from villages, mines and noble kitchens. Fees, sponsorship and refresher rotations make healing a regional profession.

the-thousandth-fall.note: Repeated training develops self-healing within an established cloister discipline. Its duration is local and does not establish the origin of other healing practices.

the-friends-i-built.note: Projection engines, dispatch slates and a three-day assessed exhibit place Cinder Annex beside advanced applied schooling. Living moss collaborators have needs and choices of their own; the infernal site’s material coordinate and side of zero remain open.

the-door-knows-home.note: Phones, a freezer and a hotplate coexist with estate appraisal, certified craft and a traveling door. The family’s property and repair problem belongs to an everyday magical modernity.

an-ordinary-education.note: Phones, buses, laboratory biotechnology and recognized magical schooling frame Delsieno’s education. Her individual lack of magic is a biological circumstance, not evidence that public magic is declining.

not-about-that.note: Magical flight supplies deliveries, agricultural weather work and ordinary family instruction in a phone-and-tram city. Proposed in the earlier public-sky horizon before the Bay, following the supplied reading sequence without identifying Solstice’s circles.

the-small-moon-rose-first.note: Nell and Bash return to supermarkets, hospital care, online searches and train journeys. This established old low-magic endpoint precedes later gods and the Glass Sea; 617 Ravel days, their eleven- and twelve-second absences, and the four-month separation between returns keep distinct clocks.

a-knock-in-someone-elses-sleep.note: Ordinary domestic life and a former bus driver frame the private dream relay. Its sixty-year separation and the entity’s imprisonment are explicitly pre-extinction; placement beside the low-magic modernity is editorial.

a-crown-of-quiet-hours.note: Kharost’s twelve dragons rotate forty-seven fabricated royal masks across 218 years. Charter reform retires the masks and their state worship; councils, archives and separate watershed sleep works replace that arrangement. The living rulers are not conflated with Varkesh’s god.

the-peace-they-could-sleep-through.note: Varkesh’s twelve dragons form one actually divine, worshipped living guise over two centuries. Full abdication, departure and human procedures due for review after one year distinguish this experiment from Kharost’s separate masks and sleep engineering.

fifty-seven-minutes.note: A dying sea creature’s gift leaves Orselle ageless for eighty-six years before a damaged harbor rite makes her a god for fifty-seven minutes. An old relief gate and restored ritual instructions matter to the port’s survival.

head-priests-in-love.note: Brackwater’s grain traffic and waterworks cross two divine jurisdictions: protection for the moored and release for the outward-bound. Repeated joint circuits make a mature shared port culture without erasing the gods’ disagreement.

saint-and-demon.note: Older salt shelter and an institutional binding rite meet at the Salt Crucible. One valley is vitrified before a second destructive surge is stopped; that local scar is neither the named Glass Sea nor the universal extinction.

a-little-winter-for-sale.note: Qarsis already uses brine, solar stills, copper exchangers and survey instruments when an ice dragon chooses paid municipal work. This is voluntary migration into an established trade ecology, not a demonstrated flight from the Stillfire disaster.

the-night-harvest.note: Three months of monster activity create an industry inside existing roads, clinics and lamp markets. Foreign fighters bring older practical knowledge of throat nodes; local observation changes handling before the six-night crisis ends.

a-crown-for-the-endless-fire.note: A present mine intersects an older bridge and shutter system above a buried fire. Lemra still maintains it through six candle states, while aged rails and a tremor endanger the bypass. Its source remains unidentified.

the-name-the-water-took.note: An armed three-week survey approaches a hidden seed community through a mapped jungle route. The captain destroys that map before losing personal memory in an older stone pool; drying recovered objects yields only bounded, one-use sensory fragments.

stay-out-of-my-city.note: Brackenport’s battleships, phones, buses and university coexist with publicly visible powers. Its harbor ultimatum and a daughter’s departure are nine local years apart; an earlier placement than the Bay avoids presenting the cities as a proven single society.

the-attendance-ledger.note: Northbridge has phones, livestreams and modern school systems, yet its city treats magic as old stories and effects. Six months of anonymous help precede the concealed showcase fight; that explicit local condition places it beside the quieter modern settings.

the-help-network.note: Three afternoons after the showcase, contact cards begin an ordinary multilingual help network that spreads over months. It joins distinct magical practices through consent, translation and forwarding limits; this does not imply a public global institution.

solstice-evening-bell.note: Centuries after independent circles negotiated the first monarchy, Solstice has no living subjects left. The Bay permanently consumes the crown’s thirteen tones but leaves her own power. It follows the proposed public-sky horizon and precedes the Glass Sea.

the-dress-they-brought-her.note: Damaged post-battle identification turns ordinary booking marks into a false survivor claim. The supplied reading sequence places this aftermath after the Bay and before Count, with the interval unestablished; the prisoner is not Solstice.

the-count-was-131072.note: Solstice herself visits the museum centuries after the battle. The shared horizon holds one connected local arc; the museum’s pre-extinction side remains a proposal.

the-future-that-refused-us.note: Three centuries of successful prediction leave Sablewake without spare timber, staff, boats or timely medicine. Breaking the local covenant ends that guarantee, exposing the ordinary infrastructure to an uncertain future; it does not end other magic.

what-i-hate-most.note: Vantress’s council-appointed sovereign manages living shadow wards through mechanical pressure signals. A neighboring ruler’s kilns and ceramic braces reduce the bodily load during a storm; worn regional infrastructure, not fading magic, causes the crisis.

daughter-of-the-sun.note: Seven once-independent service branches were centralized in the Day of Glass, preserving the capital while destroying six cities. Four hundred years later, recovered evidence and living choices break priority control into locally governed branches.

the-way-around.note: Expedition halls and a professional recorder place Ivara inside a culture that studies older works. Azhra’s immense route rings and three surviving warning scripts precede this visit; the exact builders and coordinates remain unknown.

the-morning-her-hand-moved.note: A thousand years of ledgers support engineered towns on a colossus recorded as dead. When its hand moves, 5,281 residents relocate to forearm gardens. The origin, actual prior state and meaning of the later slowing remain uncertain.

all-accounts-due.note: The final active world still has walking cities, route dragons, living palaces, gravity craft, graft medicine and inner fire. The Array’s 302 years and Faris’s thirty-one-year accumulation end at the fixed extinction; those six roots do not classify every earlier system.

four-million-falling.note: Orison’s ancient fission reactors and powered magnetic rings sustain a city of four million in a culture that remembers magic as long dead. This metropolitan infrastructure has its own proposed horizon; smaller workshop economies nearby in the layout are not its established predecessors or successors.

the-five-minute-warranty.note: Goblin engineering sustains practical inventions with short working lives.

the-ordinary-slime.note: Observation changes how a locally ordinary organism is handled.

blade-calls-your-name.note: The blade’s stored strain, mica and circuit belong to a material craft economy. Its handling depends on worked mechanisms and local social knowledge.

four-crowns-in-hiding.note: Four sanctuary kingdoms coordinate through distinct duskglass relay practices after the sisters' home kingdom collapses.

a-crown-in-the-bargain.note: Hushglass relays, road repair and parliamentary limits make this political marriage part of a distributed civic state.

the-weight-they-never-counted.note: A caravan recognizes bodily strength the village undervalued.

coiled-together.note: The serpentfolk queen's care is a local bodily and cultural fact.

the-last-monster.note: A lost adventurer and the dungeon’s inhabitants negotiate local territory through bodily capacities and practical action. The represented conflict requires no operative enchantment.

the-walls-are-thick-enough.note: An imperial marriage and garden encounter join household privacy to palace authority. The represented action requires no operative enchantment.

the-door-in-the-ivy.note: Clarimond retakes her capital seventeen years after leaving.

late-for-dinner.note: The general’s household and legion join domestic relationships to imperial military authority. The practical action fits the material palace period.

save-that-dragon.note: A queen’s rescue request belongs to a palace and dynastic setting. Ropes and winches ground the work physically; the material-zero placement remains tentative because the dragon’s fire is unclassified.

golden-lion.note: The cane exposes surviving people behind a supposedly extinct House.

the-courtesy-of-blades.note: The duel and courtship belong to an established culture of blades and conventions.

only-eighteen.note: Almost two centuries of caregiving precede eighteen human years with the twins.

the-rule-between-courses.note: Catfolk instincts and the restaurant's inherited rule form a local biological and social history.

everyone-knows-her.note: An annual urban festival frames an ordinary recognition puzzle.

before-she-gets-tired.note: Friends discuss an ordinary romantic decision.

the-names-on-the-cups.note: Hinge's story runs from early autumn to the first Sunday in May.

empire-within.note: The crime boss's three sleepless days belong to a material political modernity.

the-other-twin.note: The siblings' shared body and puberty belong to an ordinary embodied modernity.

the-station-between.note: Ruth’s familiar material-life endpoint is tentatively placed beside the ordinary modern streets. The afterlife station remains separately undated and is not a magical event inside material zero.

the-ten-thousand-year-queen.note: Merneith awakens roughly ten thousand years after the last pharaoh was entombed, following nineteen years of genetic development. Her awakening begins a sixty-year career of infrastructure and empire-building. The age of her own ancient genetic sources is a separate question; reconstruction supplies neither ancient memories nor resurrection.

terms-at-four.note: An orbital platform supplies leverage during a domestic tea party. Mature engineering extends private political power beyond an otherwise familiar household setting.

the-mercy-circuit.note: Bionic and implant repair requires a mature service economy. The repair work places manufactured embodiment within ordinary neighborhood institutions.

sakura-hearted.note: A human engineer rebuilds the moon ride from a date ten years earlier for the couple's eighth anniversary. The machinery places this household among familiar technical lives.

a-little-more-room.note: The android neighbor's arrival develops through hallway encounters.

the-unfixed-face.note: Widely available genetic modification is an established consumer practice. Medical commerce makes bodily identity a routine social and technical question.

the-kill-she-wouldnt-take.note: Televised combat and bodily rebuilding imply mature engineered public life.

deja-vu-too-late.note: An orbital cargo tug operates among occupied service infrastructure, refinery traffic and docking hazards. Its one-charge neural baseline is flight-safety equipment: restoring the pilot leaves external momentum, other people and the loss unchanged.

drone-down.note: Police drones are routine enough to produce a teenage counterculture.

the-driver-the-city-could-not-see.note: An unregistered passenger exposes an autonomous city's limits.

the-foundations-remember.note: The active rail line and neural extraction belong to a city denying older civilizations.

the-thirteenth-command.note: The combat-controller update is an engineered event.

what-she-remembered-of-peace.note: Android rehabilitation precedes renewed war and old programming.

the-body-called-one.note: Four years in Unit 02 precede extraction and a courier flight.

last-watcher-of-jupiter.note: A thirty-year Jovian watch depends on repaired machinery; an eight-year-old analog repair resists an unclassified recovery signal.

the-room-that-waited.note: A modernity falls without firing its arsenal; agrarian descendants enter the sealed room.

leave-the-names.note: The salvage code is older than the caravan's dead cities.

the-lights-beyond.note: After five hundred years of closed borders following a local war, scouts encounter a neighboring city with electric transport, illuminated streets and commercial seaplanes. Unequal contemporaries fit this modern horizon; the story does not establish a fallen technological civilization.

the-city-of-eleven-foundations.note: Many architectural and technological styles coexist in one city.

rooms-before-sunrise.note: A census refresh erases five housing bindings while their residents remain alive. Engineered living apartments enforce those records, placing this city beside other societies governed by registration and administrative visibility, without making their systems or governments identical.

the-unfixed-song.note: Generations of routes precede the archive's standardization offer.

laughing-clouds.note: The annual festival implies mature engineering and a history of repurposed failures.

kite-letters-below.note: A station teaches that the surface died 812 years ago. Ground-grown reeds answer orbital radiator vanes in inherited service script.

apes-in-orbit.note: A dinosaur polity lives under human stations whose obsolete descent coordinates endanger its hatcheries; their shared present is established, their separation undated.

the-shadow-that-nested.note: An ancient sunshade supports a living migration.

the-star-that-followed-the-bells.note: Pastoral Ruskala uses bells and radios beneath a living starship's damaged route memory. Placed after the fast-road collapse as a proposed history of fragmented travel.

the-first-people.note: The courier reaches humanity as the makers of ancient stellar roads.

the-sky-remembers-us-return.note: Ordinary light crosses the entire Long Dark from the All Accounts aftermath. The boundary is the first reciprocal link: new magic begins and no old root is restored. The displayed horizon is schematic, not a date for every earlier scene.

there-goes-your-name.note: The theft and chosen name belong to a pastoral locality with active magic.

the-hollow-cask.note: A twelve-week reopening plan meets living Underbreath in old timber.

where-no-unicorn-stands.note: The queen’s active magic and storm wards operate within hereditary rule. Her court fits the ritual kingdoms’ regional political scale after reawakening.

a-throne-neither-wanted.note: Three centuries of forecasting records precede roughly a year of suspended injury.

the-kingdom-was-the-easy-part.note: The adventurers’ retired life follows public victories in a magical kingdom. Lantern lights sustained by breath and attention place the frame outside material zero; its attachment to the renewed ritual kingdoms is proposed.

friends-of-the-night.note: Six years of proximity precede Shalegate's three-night siege.

a-darkness-written-under-skin.note: Dye workshops, an inspection lamp and a clinical graft practitioner operate within an explicit universal birth-channel convention. That population condition warrants a distinct horizon; its proposed order relative to the eighteenth-year society establishes no shared mechanism.

anatomy-of-a-god.note: Twelve years of practical treatment and regeneration experience guide a worker’s response to a divine claimant. A sanctuary, manual tools and bounded bodily knowledge supply the craft-era context; the claim does not establish a shared pantheon.

deaths-patron.note: A stair-hoist repairer and forty spellwrights’ demonstration engine place divine action inside a technically developed city. The god needs a living patron, and his seven-minute crisis retains that bounded civic mechanism.

the-players-above.note: Mill repair, couriers and route experiments give residents practical means to confront the growing machine. This active-era attachment is tentative; the machine’s ontology and its apparent players’ external coordinate remain unknown.

what-the-town-owed-her.note: Generations of obligations precede the town's encounter with its youthful witch.

the-inheritance-remembers.note: The threshold working activates during demolition in a developed civic world.

the-last-bus-to-briar-hill.note: A contemporary bus journey encounters route conditions held by local custodians. Ordinary transport meets a particular older working; neither the route’s origin nor another gate’s date is established.

the-cat-who-had-enough.note: The inherited cat's advice belongs to an established household arrangement.

the-trouble-with-tuesdays.note: Forty-six activations, seven Tuesdays to the audit and Rose's later nine-day overwrite keep one family sequence.

gods-afraid-of-grandma.note: The grandmother’s continued earthly life involves particular gods inside familiar domestic routines. The encounter supplies no general public account of divine involvement.

the-night-she-knew.note: Clairvoyance is known privately in one contemporary family. That local knowledge fits this proposed horizon without proving powers are absent from public institutions elsewhere.

self-reflection.note: Anin’s independent life lasts four dawns in a modern household. The family confronts an unexplained local event; its wider occurrence and origin remain unsettled.

thirteen-years-borrowed.note: Thirteen years of searching end in a bounded encounter through a living host.

the-wrong-side-of-the-part.note: An unfamiliar wig changes its wearer within ordinary modern life. This private encounter fits the horizon of locally held knowledge, while the object’s maker and earlier history remain unknown.

roads-under-impossible-stars.note: A familiar road trip changes beneath an anomalous sky. Only its living departure frame is tentatively placed here; altered routes and experienced reversals retain unsettled clocks.

by-tooth-and-threshold.note: A visitor arrives days after the trapped wolf’s rescue, revealing an identity previously unknown to the rescuer. The local disclosure does not establish universal secrecy or date another nonhuman community.

the-bat-at-the-door.note: The daughter’s care for a bat precedes the visitors’ godparent request. An unexpected identity enters one modern household’s knowledge, without establishing a public supernatural institution.

the-wolf-in-the-mirror.note: A recurring full-moon change is managed through a partner’s private knowledge and household preparations. Other communities’ knowledge and the transformation’s earlier history remain open.

she-literally-has-wings.note: Grown, inherited and built wings are ordinary recognized possibilities in Coralie’s community. That public recognition places her household alongside other civic accommodations, while her personal identity still requires a conversation.

the-one-who-gets-tired.note: The gods deliberately present themselves as ordinary Cusco neighbors and their children practice human routines. That specific concealment fits this horizon; the oldest sibling’s limits remain personal.

a-place-for-the-living.note: Decades-dead relatives visit during one first family dinner.

transitions-in-common.note: A student explicitly keeps shapeshifting an impossible secret unknown at school. This documented concealment distinguishes the local context from communities where multiple bodily origins are publicly ordinary; their wider historical relationship remains proposed.

realms.note: Licensed exit staff and a clinic beside the return tunnel provide screened treatment and monitoring. This human care frame fits a context of practical services around unusual crossings; Deepmarket keeps an open coordinate, and specialist care here does not date an unprepared clinic elsewhere.

his-infernal-majesty-says-no.note: A regulated private infernal gate reaches a contemporary engineering college. The human frame belongs to the negotiated-crossing era; the infernal realm gains no planetary date.

the-warmest-person-in-the-room.note: The superhero college already teaches a cursed prodigy.

captive-couples.note: Established hero and villain identities shape two marriages.

the-name-i-kept.note: A hero family has already disowned an older sibling.

witch-cold.note: An illness brings uncontrolled workings into a friend’s home, where agreed signals, adapted equipment and ordinary nursing advice support care. A working outfit and noisy jobs do not establish a hero college or agency; everyday accommodation is the stronger social context.

ultimate-evil-dog.note: The villain's transformation turns attempted infiltration into domestic life.

life-with-a-girlfriend-with-shrinking-po.note: A couple uses radios, adapted tools and explicit procedures to accommodate shrinking in a modern apartment. Their household can coexist with organized public power; the equipment and limits do not establish a universal capacity.

where-sleep-takes-you.note: A purpose-built onset and location tag helps with involuntary travel, and building staff respond through identification and recorded times. connections.note: Proposed historical sequence: the destruction of universal fast transit is followed by a reach in which stellar travel is fragmented, represented here by the damaged ship over Ruskala and its independent satellite flock. The root burn does not explain the ship's memory damage, and no common route technology is established. The proposed inheritance is a disconnected sky in which local navigation matters again.

connections.label: A profession reaching beyond the city
connections.note: Proposed regional connection: Lanternscrape receives three qualified surveyors with distinct instruments, while the municipal licensing story tests practice against pipe loads and source limits. These are compatible city-and-periphery conditions for circulating technical skills. A shared professional culture is plausible; the same guild, licensing law or exact date is not established.

connections.label: From taught flight to an inhabited sky
connections.note: Proposed long development: Nine Eaves already teaches roof-level flight and survey work using several kinds of focus; the later public sky uses diverse living flight in deliveries, family instruction and agricultural weather. The bridge is the spread of practical aerial knowledge through teaching and work, not a common power source or proof that one academy founded that city.

connections.label: Dragon service beyond hereditary alliance
connections.note: Proposed change in regional political economy: noble-dragon agreements exchange watch, rescue, nesting care and water access, while Qarsis hires a voluntarily migrant ice dragon for bounded municipal work among condensers and trade routes. The comparison supports a later reach where some dragon services travel as paid expertise. It does not claim all alliances ended or that Urumet descends from the earlier partners.

connections.label: Who controls the living heat?
connections.note: Proposed technical connection: Vantress combines living shadow, mineral heat, ceramic braces and ordinary pressure signals; the Glass-Sea branches combine dusk, living solar fire and physical heat-and-water conduits. Methods for sharing loads and limiting a capital’s draw could circulate between such societies. This proposes a field of civic engineering, not identical magic, named teachers or a proven order between the two regions.
